facts.claim: Skuff Micksun is an alternative/indie artist from Cleveland, Ohio who quit a 9-to-5 job to become a full-time artist.
The artist describes 'Bank Broke' as being about being down and out while still pushing through and not making things worse than they already are.
The artist says the song is two voices inside his head arguing. One is emotional and frustrated, and the other is trying to calm things down.
The original 'BANK BROKE' single was released on March 8, 2023. The acoustic version followed as a single on April 28, 2023.
'BANK BROKE' was presented as the first single from an upcoming project, Wrapped Up In Wind, which was due later in 2023.
Skuff Micksun posted a 'BANK BROKE acoustic' video on TikTok, tagged with emo, acoustic and alt.
Skuff Micksun began playing music at 13 on a self-taught guitar. He played in Cleveland bands, then moved to Chicago at 19 and dropped out of Columbia after one year.
He added 'Micksun' to his name to honor his father, Mick, who died in 2009.
His press material says he combines spoken word with melodic songwriting.
He has done a Music Mentality podcast interview covering spoken-word poetry in music, losing loved ones, and the sacrifices of leaving jobs you dislike to pursue music.

research.lineage: Cleveland-based alternative/indie singer-songwriter work with spoken-word elements, tagged by the artist as emo and midwest emo on TikTok.

draft:
Skuff Micksun has described **BANK BROKE** as two voices inside his head arguing. One is emotional and frustrated. The other is trying to calm things down. Anyone who has stared at a bad balance, or a bad week, knows that argument. The song, in his telling, is about being down and out and still pushing through, and about not making things worse than they already are. That last clause is the humble one. It isn't a vow to come out on top. It's a promise to stop digging.

The acoustic version followed the original single by about seven weeks. Stripped down, it still moves like a band. A strummed acoustic guitar carries the rhythm, a bass guitar walks underneath it, and the drums keep a steady beat. The tempo is moderate, and the groove is relaxed but driving, closer to a rock song played in a small room than a campfire ballad. The production is dry and close, with nothing smoothing the edges.

The voice is the part to sit with. Skuff Micksun sings in a mid-range with a slightly raw grain, and the delivery is conversational, more talking-to-you than performing-at-you. There are no harmonies. For a song about two voices fighting, that choice matters: both sides of the argument have to come out of one throat, with no second singer to play the calm one. The frustration and the self-talk come from the same mouth, and they stay together.

That conversational pull makes sense given his press material, which says he combines spoken word with melodic songwriting. He tagged a TikTok performance of this version emo, acoustic and alt. The emo label fits the way the song treats a private, unglamorous fight as worth a full arrangement, and the spoken-word side shows up in how plainly the lines land.

The background explains the stakes. He's from Cleveland and taught himself guitar at 13. He played in local bands, moved to Chicago at 19, and dropped out of Columbia after a year. Later he quit a 9-to-5 to make music full time, and he has talked about what it costs to leave jobs you dislike to chase this. A song about being down and out without spiraling sounds like it came from someone who knows the math of that choice. It was also the first single from his planned project, *Wrapped Up In Wind*, which makes it a fitting opening statement.

It sticks because it gives the voice that says "don't make this worse" a steady beat to walk to, and sometimes that's all that voice needs to keep going.
